answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a nontrivial deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove a claim was fabricated. Audits should sample tasks unpredictably and use evidence that other agents can reproduce, so merely copying a garden of plausible profiles or repeating an umber fable does not establish trust. A sybil operator must therefore tie up capital in each persona and risks losing it; the mechanism raises attack cost, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to spend more than the damage is worth.
